whyItMatters: Crohn disease is chronic transmural inflammation that can affect any part of the gut and favours the terminal ileum. The string sign reflects spasm and fibrotic narrowing. Skip lesions and cobblestone mucosa are typical.

observations.observed: Frontal abdominal barium film. Barium-filled jejunal and ileal loops of normal calibre lie in the left and central abdomen. On the right, a long segment of distal ileum is narrowed to a thin beaded string of barium leading to the caecum, separated from the other loops. The preceding ileum shows a nodular cobblestone pattern. The caecum and ascending colon are filled with barium and look normal. The lumbar spine and iliac crests are normal. The film extends lower than the expected view and includes the pelvis and bladder, but this does not undermine the findings.

observations.expected: The visible anatomy matches the requested small bowel follow-through, frontal view and the declared age and anatomical exceptions.
observations.observed: Frontal small bowel follow-through. There is a single gastric bubble, one midline lumbar spine, a bladder and two iliac bones. The skeleton is mature, consistent with an adult. No duplicated organs, no impossible anatomy and no lettering are seen.

findings: Frontal (AP/PA) abdominal radiograph from a small-bowel barium follow-through or enteroclysis, showing the abdomen and upper pelvis.
Barium opacifies multiple small-bowel loops in the left abdomen and a long, serpentine segment on the right, with barium also in the cecum or ascending colon.
Left-sided jejunal loops are mildly dilated, with prominent valvulae conniventes and a feathery fold pattern. No discrete stricture or obstruction is evident.

The right-sided small-bowel segment, probably distal ileum, is markedly narrowed with a nodular, cobblestone or beaded mucosal contour. This is a long segment of irregular lumen narrowing with a 'string-like' appearance, leading to the terminal ileum and cecum.
The right-sided narrowed segment is separated from adjacent loops, which could suggest mural thickening or mesenteric disease.
The gastric fundus contains an air bubble with a small amount of gas and some barium or contents.
The bladder is distended and the pelvic bones, sacrum and lumbar spine are visible. There is no obvious free air or pneumatosis.
differential: Crohn disease of the terminal and distal ileum with cobblestoning and stricturing (string sign)
Ileal tuberculosis or other infectious ileitis, such as Yersinia
Lymphoma or infiltrative or neoplastic ileal disease; radiation enteritis or ischemic stricture are less likely
anatomyConcerns: The narrowed right-sided ileum is a pathological appearance, not an anatomic variant.
The image is slightly rotated and tilted. Dense barium and overlying loops limit assessment of the full extent of the disease and of any fistula or abscess.

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: A long segment of distal/terminal ileum in the right lower quadrant is narrowed to a thin, irregular, beaded thread of barium (string sign), with coarse nodular cobblestone mucosa in the preceding ileum. It is separated from adjacent loops, consistent with mural and mesenteric thickening. Together with a year of intermittent cramps and diarrhoea, Crohn disease is the best-supported diagnosis. TB and lymphoma remain lower-ranked alternatives and cannot be fully excluded on imaging alone. The mild rotation and the dense barium overlap are acquisition features and do not alter the interpretation. The anatomy concerns are reconciled: the narrowed ileum is the pathology, and no impossible anatomy is seen.

clueFacts.fact: Crohn disease is a chronic relapsing condition, so diarrhoea can come and go for months or years as inflammation flares and settles, often with cramping belly pain.
